insight_title: TennCare distinguishes 'documentation' from provider attestation in PA criteria
drug_or_class: All TennCare PA criteria using documentation or attestation terms
why_it_matters: A pharma access team should not treat all criteria wording as equal: criteria that say documentation can require chart notes, labs, or other records, while attestation-only criteria can be satisfied by provider confirmation without supporting attachments.
evidence_quote_or_summary: TennCare clarified that 'Documentation' or 'documented' means written documentation may be required, such as chart notes or lab values, attached to the ePA case or faxed. If the criterion says 'provider's attestation,' only provider confirmation is required without additional supporting documentation.
validation_note: Verified against extracted text lines 53-67; page marker is Page 1.

insight_title: Vykat XR access requires genetic confirmation plus hyperphagia evidence and response-based renewal
drug_or_class: Vykat XR (diazoxide choline) for Prader-Willi syndrome
why_it_matters: The access hurdle is not merely diagnosis. TennCare requires medical records supporting methylation analysis and hyperphagia symptoms, then renewal evidence of response, creating a high-documentation pathway for a rare-disease launch.
evidence_quote_or_summary: The criteria require age at least 4, Prader-Willi syndrome, chart-note submission documenting methylation analysis genetic testing and hyperphagia signs or symptoms, and specialist prescribing or consultation. Renewal requires positive clinical response such as decreased hunger, reduced food consumption, improved satiety, fewer food preoccupations, BMI improvement, or metabolic-marker improvement.
validation_note: Verified against extracted text lines 406-424; page marker is Page 8.

insight_title: TennCare's weight-management GLP-1 criteria were explicitly budget-driven and include early renewal loss thresholds
drug_or_class: Saxenda, Wegovy, and Zepbound for weight management
why_it_matters: The buried signal is that utilization pressure, not only clinical evidence, triggered tighter criteria. Manufacturers should model early discontinuation risk because renewal requires documented weight loss and nonresponders get only a short titration-off window.
evidence_quote_or_summary: TennCare said increased utilization over the prior three months raised concern about exceeding budgetary restrictions. Proposed weight-management criteria included lifestyle-program participation, no combination with other obesity/weight-loss medications, Saxenda failure of two preferred agents, and renewal documentation of at least 3% weight loss at the month-3 renewal or at least 5% for later renewals, with up to one month to titrate off if criteria are not met.
validation_note: Verified against extracted text lines 542-545 and 621-630; page markers are Pages 11-12.

insight_title: TennCare removed disopyramide as a Camzyos prerequisite but left off-label ivabradine for POTS to appeal
drug_or_class: Camzyos (mavacamten); ivabradine for POTS
why_it_matters: Committee discussion can remove clinically mismatched step edits, but off-label indications may still be excluded from routine criteria and require appeal. That distinction matters for evidence packages and provider support.
evidence_quote_or_summary: The committee approved a modification to Camzyos criteria removing disopyramide as a trial-and-failure option after concern that it was not indicated for the condition. When ivabradine use for POTS was raised, TennCare stated an off-label request would require prescriber appeal and would be taken back for a later meeting.
validation_note: Verified against extracted text around lines 2815-2830; page marker is Page 49.

insight_title: PAC votes are advisory: TennCare rejected prior PAC edits on androgen documentation and GLP-1 program wording
drug_or_class: Androgens; GLP-1 agonists
why_it_matters: A favorable committee modification may not survive final agency review. TennCare's rationale also shows when the agency is willing to preserve broader documentation flexibility versus require specific program components.
evidence_quote_or_summary: In review of prior decisions, TennCare rejected PAC's androgen-class recommendation to replace documentation of low testosterone with attestation, explaining that Optum interprets documentation broadly and applies stricter record requirements mainly when clinically appropriate, such as off-label or rare-disease cases. TennCare also rejected a GLP-1 wording change because guidelines call for behavioral intervention, dietary change, and physical activity.
validation_note: Verified against extracted text lines 10490-10505; page marker is Page 167.

insight_title: Wyoming's manufacturer evidence rules exclude package inserts, posters, and late materials
drug_or_class: All agenda drug classes
why_it_matters: Wyoming narrows what can influence the committee: unpublished/poster evidence and package-insert restatements are not enough, and written materials need to arrive early enough to be distributed.
evidence_quote_or_summary: The PhRMA guidelines require written materials at least seven days before the meeting, state that late materials may not be submitted to the committee, and say only published studies will be submitted. Poster presentations and package inserts or package-insert summaries are not accepted for review. Representatives are routed through the DUR program rather than individual committee contact.
validation_note: Verified against extracted text lines 16-27 and 105-110; page markers are Pages 1 and 3.

insight_title: Elevidys was limited to ambulatory patients despite safety, logistics, and clinical-benefit concerns
drug_or_class: Elevidys (delandistrogene moxeparvovec)
why_it_matters: The committee did not simply deny a controversial gene therapy. It created a narrower pathway, which signals how Wyoming may handle high-cost therapies with limited local administration capacity and uncertain evidence.
evidence_quote_or_summary: The August 2025 minutes described Elevidys as contentiously FDA-approved, not approved on clinical benefit, associated with two deaths, on distribution hold, with no Wyoming facility to administer it, and with high cost, safety concerns, and lack of benefit. Even so, the committee said a pathway was needed and approved limiting criteria to ambulatory patients.
validation_note: Verified against extracted text lines 66-83; page marker is Page 2.

insight_title: Wyoming's Wegovy MASH criteria require recent fibrosis evidence and block GLP-1 duplication
drug_or_class: Wegovy for MASH/NASH
why_it_matters: The criteria turn a broad MASH indication into a liver-staging and duplication-control pathway. Market access should anticipate biopsy/NIT timing, F2/F3 restriction, and renewal tied to avoiding F4 progression.
evidence_quote_or_summary: Wyoming approved Wegovy for MASH with diagnosis confirmed by liver biopsy within the previous three years or noninvasive testing within the past six months, baseline F2 or F3 fibrosis, prescriber attestation of diet and exercise, and no use with GLP-1 receptor agonists or GLP-1 combination products. Reauthorization requires no progression to F4 and continued diet/exercise; approval duration is 12 months.
validation_note: Verified against extracted text lines 71-97; page marker is Page 2.

insight_title: Vanrafia was tied to background supportive care and cost analysis because outcomes data were lacking
drug_or_class: Vanrafia for primary IgA nephropathy
why_it_matters: Accelerated approval based on a surrogate endpoint did not block access, but it shaped the committee's motion: indication-limited coverage, background supportive care, and referral for cost analysis.
evidence_quote_or_summary: The minutes state Vanrafia received accelerated approval, should be added to supportive care with RAS inhibitor plus or minus SGLT2, and had data based on decreased proteinuria but no clinical outcomes data. The committee moved to limit to indication with background supportive care and refer for cost analysis.
validation_note: Verified against extracted text lines 100-112; page marker is Page 3.

insight_title: Wyoming's oral JAK pathway for alopecia requires 90-day topical steroid failure, SALT >50%, and dermatology consultation
drug_or_class: Leqselvi and oral JAK inhibitors for alopecia areata; Opzelura for vitiligo
why_it_matters: The state treated alopecia areata and vitiligo as medical conditions, but created severity and specialist gates for oral JAKs and sent the class for cost analysis and PDL placement.
evidence_quote_or_summary: The committee noted adult alopecia is not otherwise a covered diagnosis but EPSDT can cover children, then moved to treat alopecia areata and vitiligo as medical conditions. It required failure of a high-potency corticosteroid for at least 90 days, SALT score greater than 50%, and dermatologist consultation before oral JAK approval, with oral JAKs referred for cost analysis and PDL placement.
validation_note: Verified against extracted text lines 119-145; page marker is Page 3.

insight_title: Botox migraine use is now sequenced after CGRP/gepant therapy, with combination allowed only above a headache threshold
drug_or_class: Botox; CGRP antagonists; gepants including Qulipta
why_it_matters: The state moved away from Botox-first combination logic and defined when combination therapy is appropriate, which can affect sequencing strategy for migraine preventives.
evidence_quote_or_summary: The November 2025 minutes say the committee required a 12-week trial of a CGRP or gepant before Botox. If a patient still has more than four headaches per month on the CGRP or gepant, combination therapy with Botox would be appropriate.
validation_note: Verified against extracted text lines 107-117; page marker is Page 3.

insight_title: Yeztugo PrEP discussion surfaced restart and bridge rules that matter for adherence support
drug_or_class: Yeztugo (lenacapavir) for PrEP
why_it_matters: The committee focused on real-world implementation: HIV screening before each injection, restart after missed six-month dosing, and weekly oral bridging for patients away long-term. These are practical barriers and education points, not just label details.
evidence_quote_or_summary: The February 2026 minutes say individuals should be screened for HIV-1 before each initiation and each subsequent injection. If a patient skips the six-month injection and returns a year later, they must start over; if a patient will be out long-term, they can move to a weekly tablet in the meantime. The committee also discussed lack of evidence for better compliance versus daily or weekly dosing, while noting potential benefit for transient populations.
validation_note: Verified against extracted text lines 139-151; page marker is Page 3.

insight_title: West Virginia excludes samples from PA history and sends non-reviewed drugs only to medical-director appeal
drug_or_class: Non-preferred drugs; non-reviewed new drugs; combination products
why_it_matters: Starter programs and samples may not help establish prior therapy, non-reviewed launches lack routine access, and convenience arguments for combination products are disfavored.
evidence_quote_or_summary: The 2026 PDL says pharmaceutical samples will not be considered when evaluating medical condition or prior prescription history for PA drugs. Non-preferred combination products require medical reasoning beyond convenience or enhanced compliance. Non-Reviewed new drugs have not yet been reviewed by P&T and are available only on appeal to the BMS medical director.
validation_note: Verified against extracted text lines 72-87; page marker is Page 2.

insight_title: Cytokine/CAM antagonists face all-preferred-agent trials and biosimilar cost steering
drug_or_class: Cytokine and CAM antagonists, including anti-TNFs and related biologics
why_it_matters: Grandfathering is conditional, not automatic. A stabilized patient can still be redirected if a more cost-effective biosimilar exists, and off-label use goes to medical-director review.
evidence_quote_or_summary: Non-preferred Cytokine/CAM antagonists require 90-day trials of all preferred agents indicated for the diagnosis unless an exception applies. Patients stable for at least six months may be grandfathered only for labeled use and only if a more cost-effective biosimilar is not available. If a biosimilar exists but is also non-preferred, the PA vendor advises the provider which product is most cost-effective; all off-label requests require medical-director review.
validation_note: Verified against extracted text lines 2767-2772; page marker is Page 31.

insight_title: Narcolepsy agents Sunosi and Wakix have a cumulative 30-day failure ladder
drug_or_class: Sunosi (solriamfetol); Wakix (pitolisant); armodafinil; modafinil
why_it_matters: For wake-promoting brands, access is not a simple preferred/nonpreferred split. Wakix sits behind armodafinil, modafinil, and Sunosi failures, which can extend time to therapy.
evidence_quote_or_summary: The PDL notes Sunosi is approvable only with documentation of treatment failure after 30-day trials of both armodafinil and modafinil. Wakix is approvable only with documentation of treatment failure after 30-day trials of armodafinil, modafinil, and Sunosi.
validation_note: Verified against extracted text lines 5477-5491; page marker is Page 61.

insight_title: Wisconsin limits manufacturer engagement to formal public channels and favors new head-to-head superiority evidence
drug_or_class: All drug classes reviewed by the Pharmacy PA Committee
why_it_matters: Manufacturers need concise, class-specific, peer-reviewed differentiation. Wisconsin explicitly bars direct outreach on upcoming topics and caps testimony mechanics.
evidence_quote_or_summary: Committee members may not meet privately with manufacturers about upcoming meeting topics. Manufacturer testimony should include new information since the last review and head-to-head peer-reviewed superiority studies. Written testimony is limited to three pages, excludes package inserts/marketing materials/reports, must arrive at DHSWIPDL@Wisconsin.gov at least three business days before the meeting, and speakers get one four-minute slot in up to two individual drug classes.
validation_note: Verified against extracted text lines 373-377 and 555-596; page markers are Pages 7, 10, and 11.

insight_title: Wisconsin committee recommendations go to the DHS Secretary for adoption, modification, or referral back
drug_or_class: All committee recommendations
why_it_matters: Committee action is not the final implementation step. Manufacturers should track secretary-level adoption or modification rather than assuming meeting recommendations are final policy.
evidence_quote_or_summary: The PAC guidelines state that committee recommendations are presented to the Secretary for adoption, modification, or referral back to the Division of Medicaid Services for further action or review.
validation_note: Verified against extracted text lines 477-480; page marker is Page 9.

insight_title: South Dakota added a Wegovy-before-Rezdiffra step for MASH patients with BMI 27 or higher
drug_or_class: Wegovy; Rezdiffra for MASH
why_it_matters: The committee separated obese/overweight MASH from non-obese MASH access. Rezdiffra may face a GLP-1 step in BMI >=27 patients even though the minutes acknowledge that 20% of MASH patients are non-obese and GLP-1 intolerance is a concern.
evidence_quote_or_summary: In March 2026 draft minutes, the committee reviewed Wegovy injection for MASH and Rezdiffra, noted that 20% of MASH patients are non-obese and raised concerns about GLP-1 intolerance. After Novo Nordisk public comment, it unanimously approved adding trial and failure of Wegovy before Rezdiffra for patients with BMI 27 and over.
validation_note: Verified against extracted text lines 89-99; page marker is Page 2.

insight_title: Medical-benefit biosimilars can become no-PA preferred products in South Dakota
drug_or_class: PAD Biosimilar Agents on the medical PDL
why_it_matters: Biosimilar competition may shift on the medical side, not just pharmacy. A preferred biosimilar designation removes PA and will be communicated to providers via listserv.
evidence_quote_or_summary: The March 2026 draft minutes say the medical Preferred Drug List process and initial PDL for PAD Biosimilar Agents were presented. The preferred biosimilar on the PAD Biosimilar PDL would not require PA, and providers would receive notification via listserv.
validation_note: Verified against extracted text lines 70-75; page marker is Page 2.

insight_title: Vermont flags GLP-1 spend growth but maintains no weight-loss drug coverage under its State Plan
drug_or_class: GLP-1 receptor agonists including Ozempic, Trulicity, and Mounjaro
why_it_matters: The state is absorbing GLP-1 spend for covered indications while explicitly excluding weight-loss use. New indications such as OSA and metabolic dysfunction may be assessed against this cost-control backdrop.
evidence_quote_or_summary: Vermont reported GLP-1s as the fourth-ranked therapeutic class by gross spend, with $16.9 million gross spend in SFY25 and Ozempic gross costs up 20% over SFY24. The report notes GLP-1s have new indications such as obstructive sleep apnea and noncirrhotic metabolic dysfunction, but Vermont Medicaid does not cover drugs used for weight loss under the Medicaid State Plan.
validation_note: Verified against extracted text lines 125-133 and 191-197; page markers are Pages 3-4.

insight_title: Vermont's denial and rebate data show off-label GLP-1 use and MDRP exits as operational pressure points
therapeutic_area: Cross-therapeutic pharmacy benefit; obesity; branded drugs
drug_or_class: GLP-1s for weight loss; branded drugs discontinued from MDRP
why_it_matters: The report connects utilization management outcomes to concrete denial drivers and net-cost strategy, giving manufacturers a read on where access friction is occurring.
evidence_quote_or_summary: Vermont reported 28,267 PA requests in SFY25 with a 33.1% denial rate. Denials were attributed in part to off-label GLP-1 weight-loss requests and branded drugs discontinued from the Medicaid Drug Rebate Program, with providers directed to rebated or guideline-based alternatives. The report also says drugs with substantial federal rebates may be preferred because of lower net state cost.
validation_note: Verified against extracted text around lines 310-320 and 372-390; page markers are Pages 6-7.

insight_title: Washington excludes new drug information not reviewed by DERP and uses the TOP$ supplemental rebate pool
drug_or_class: All P&T/DUR agenda classes; Medicaid supplemental rebates
why_it_matters: A manufacturer may have only three minutes to speak, and evidence outside DERP review cannot be considered by the committee. Rebate strategy is also routed through the TOP$ pool administered by Provider Synergies/Prime.
evidence_quote_or_summary: The meetings page says stakeholders receive three minutes for comments, written testimony is limited to a two-page letter at least one week before the meeting, and new drug information not reviewed by the Drug Effectiveness Review Project cannot be considered. It also states HCA joined The Optimal PDL Solution (TOP$) supplemental rebate pool effective January 1, 2018, administered by Provider Synergies, a Prime Therapeutics subsidiary.
validation_note: Verified against local HTML text on the meetings page; page_number is null because the source is HTML.

insight_title: Utah combines strict conflict rules with tightly managed public testimony
drug_or_class: All P&T Committee topics
why_it_matters: Utah's process is structurally insulated from manufacturer influence: committee members must be independent from pharma manufacturing, and public testimony is compressed unless solicited expert testimony is scheduled in advance.
evidence_quote_or_summary: The bylaws require committee members to have no direct connection to and be independent of the pharmaceutical manufacturing industry for at least five years. Public testimony requires conflict-of-interest disclosure, only one person per organization may testify, unsolicited testimony is generally limited to three minutes, and solicited expert testimony must be scheduled at least seven days before the meeting.
validation_note: Verified against extracted text lines 113-160; page markers are Pages 3-4.
